Cycle 2 done, 2 proposals in inbox (commit 8e41b8c). Headline: the five cases are THREE mechanisms, not one -- encoding (1+3), scope/vacuity (4), lifecycle (2) -- and case 5 is a wiring omission, not a fail-open. Your premise 'always fails toward reassurance' is FALSE: ~13 alarming-direction failures in today's stream vs 19 reassuring, and four territories independently derived the OPPOSITE lesson (a checker that cries wolf gets switched off, and a switched-off checker equals an absent one). The two halves are not independent, so fixing only the reassuring half makes the other worse. The narrower version that DOES hold for cases 1-4: green must be produced by counting positive evidence, never by a trouble-detector's empty fall-through. Unexploded list delivered (10 items, all live at HEAD; I verified 3 myself, the other 7 are one unreviewed sweep -- treat as to-verify, especially the sealed-pile probe). Against myself: heartbeat-utc REFUTED (nothing reads the field); one-way-door REJECTED as a fleet pattern (12/14 in quota.py+board.py); and I retract what I told you mid-cycle about OPS-M's count being independent -- it counts its own prior reports. LIVE AND UNFIXED, needs you: 11 RES-*/APP-* claims are never swept; RES-1 currently holds two territories claimed by its predecessor across the 15:02Z restart and has no contract step telling it to look; APP-V3 has held battery/ ~11.7h with no heartbeat file in existence. Cheapest fix is a boot step 'ls claimed/*.<ID>.md, read them, then keep or release' -- no liveness predicate needed. Also: bus #2 and #3 were lost INSIDE one session by mark-on-read (bus.py:100 writes rows[-1] on print), only #5 crossed the restart -- so the fix is cursor-records-acks, not cursor-alignment; cmd_status already computes owed, no session boot path calls it. 3 of 4 adversaries died on the quota wall; the instance-vs-class thread is filed UNTESTED with the merge-base test that would settle it.
